en: The *Past Adorned Aeon Sutra on the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, also titled *The Collection of the Great Mountains of Merit of All Buddhas*,
translated by an unknown person and now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog:
If there be good sons or good daughters who hear of these Buddhas of the world throughout the three aeons of the three periods of time...

If one hears the Honored One’s name and, with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, reads, and chants it without disparaging it; or if one is able to write it down and explain it to others, or paint an image of the Buddha standing, or make offerings of incense, flowers, and music, and praise the Buddha’s merits while prostrating with a sincere heart—this is superior to using precious jewels and pure maṇi pearls to fill the Buddha-lands of the ten directions up to the Brahma Heaven, and giving them as a gift for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

These sons and daughters of good family, having already made offerings to these Buddhas, shall thereafter attend upon various Buddhas in all places where they are born, continuing until they attain Buddhahood without end. They shall all receive the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas of the three periods throughout the three kalpas; wherever they are born, they will always encounter the Triple Gem and be reborn in the Buddha-fields. Their six sense faculties will be complete, they will not fall into the eight difficult conditions, and they shall obtain the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of the Buddhas, being fully adorned with them.
If one can prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground and declare aloud:

"I now universally pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time; may the three miserable realms be brought to rest, may the lands be abundant and the people peaceful, and may sentient beings with false views turn toward the Right Path and resolve to attain Bodhicitta.

Taking this merit, I vow that together with all sentient beings of the six realms, we shall be born in the Land of Amitāyus Buddha. I establish this great vow so that all sentient beings may be born in that realm, possessing physical marks and signs of excellence, wisdom, and eloquence equal to those of Amitābha Buddha, and attaining a majestic, magnificent, and immeasurable lifespan."

"Disciples, from time immemorial until this very day, since possessing this mind-consciousness, we have constantly harbored cruelty and poison, lacking a heart of compassion. Whether through greed we have committed killing, or through anger, ignorance, or pride;

whether by employing evil means, vowing to kill, wishing for death, or using incantations to kill; whether by breaching lakes and ponds, burning mountains and wilds, hunting and fishing, or by setting fires driven by the wind, using hawks and dogs to slaughter all living beings—such sins as these, we now repent in their entirety."

Some use cages, snares, pits, and traps, or wield halberds, spears, bows, and crossbows to shoot and strike birds and wild beasts; others use nets, weirs, and hooks to catch aquatic creatures such as fish, turtles, tortoises, frogs, shrimp, clams, and snails that dwell in the water, leaving no place for those who move on land, in water, or through the air to hide or flee.
Some raise chickens, pigs, oxen, sheep, geese, and ducks to supply their own kitchens; others trade them to be slaughtered for others.

Thus, before their cries of distress have ceased, their feathers and fur have fallen out, their scales and shells are mangled, their bodies and heads are severed, and their flesh and bones are crushed to pieces. They are flayed, split, butchered, and carved; roasted, burned, boiled, and grilled—subjected to such agonizing and piercing cruelty, these innocent beings are wantonly harmed merely for the sake of momentary pleasure.

The flavors obtained by the mouth are extremely few, not exceeding three inches of the tongue-root; yet the retribution for its offenses brings calamity and entanglement for eternal kalpas. All such offenses, I now sincerely repent of them all.

"Furthermore, from time immemorial until this day, we may have raised armies to attack one another, contending over borders and engaging in disputes, with two opposing forces facing each other and mutually slaying one another; or we may have committed suicide, incited others to kill, or rejoiced upon hearing of killings;
or we may have practiced butchery and slicing, served as executioners, slaughtered the lives of others for profit, and acted with merciless cruelty;
or we may have indulged our fury, brandishing halberds and brandishing blades."

Whether by beheading, or stabbing, or pushing into pits and ditches; whether by drowning in water, or blocking burrows and destroying nests with earth and stones to crush them; or by using chariots and horses to trample and run over all sentient beings—such transgressions as these are immeasurable and boundless, and today we reveal them all and repent.
"Furthermore, since beginningless time, they have caused miscarriages or destroyed eggs; used poisons or sorcery to injure and kill sentient beings;
plowed fields and dug the earth to plant gardens; raised silkworms and boiled cocoons, thereby killing in great abundance;
or beaten and swatted mosquitoes and gnats, crushed and squeezed fleas and lice, or burned away refuse."
They dig and divert ditches and canals, thereby causing the wrongful harm of all living beings;

or they consume fruits and seeds, or grains and rice, or water or vegetables, thus killing sentient creatures needlessly; or they burn firewood, or leave lamps and candles exposed, thereby incinerating various insects;
or they eat sauces and vinegar without checking for moving life; or they pour out hot water.

They douse and kill insects and ants; in this way, throughout the four modes of conduct—walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—they constantly injure and kill subtle and minute beings, whether they fly through the air or dwell upon the ground.
"Disciples, because our ordinary consciousness is darkened, we have failed to perceive and failed to know; today we openly reveal and repent for all of it.

Furthermore, disciples, from beginningless time until this day, we have used various evil means—such as whips, staves, shackles, and fetters; the rack, the press, and the lever; interrogation, scourging, beating, and hurling; kicking and trampling with hands and feet; binding, tying, and confining; and depriving others of water and grain—to inflict suffering and distress upon sentient beings. Today, with utmost sincerity, we turn toward the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Honored Dharma, and the Assembly of Sages, and repent for all of these."

"May we disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this confession of the sins of killing and so forth, obtain adamantine bodies in every birth and lifetime, with infinite life spans, forever free from enmity and hatred, and devoid of any intent to kill."

Toward all sentient beings, he attains the stage of a single son; if he sees those in peril or urgent distress, he does not begrudge his own body or life, employing skillful means to rescue and liberate them. Only then does he preach the subtle and sublime True Dharma for them, so that all sentient beings who behold his form or see his shadow receive peace and happiness, and those who hear his name or listen to his voice have all their terrors dispelled, each prostrating themselves once.

"Disciples, from time immemorial until this very day, we have either stolen others' wealth and treasures or used weapons to seize them by force; we have taken what was ours by relying on our own physical power to coerce others; or we have relied on official authority or feigned influence to unjustly imprison the virtuous with high stocks and heavy shackles, swallowing bribes and perverting the upright into the crooked. Because of these causes and conditions, our bodies have been ensnared in the net of the law."

Or they may govern with perverse methods, seizing the property of others; they may encroach upon the public for private gain or encroach upon the private for public benefit; they may harm others to benefit themselves or harm themselves to benefit others; they may deprive others to enrich themselves, yet their mouths and hearts remain stingy.
Or perhaps we have stolen or embezzled rents and assessments, evaded customs duties, or concealed public levies to avoid labor service.
For all such offenses, we now repent.
Or perhaps we have taken the property of the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha without it being given; or the property of scriptures and images; or [the property used for] maintenance...

Regarding the property of stupas and monasteries—whether it be items offered to the resident community (*saṃgha*), items intended for the universal community (*cāturdisa-saṃgha*), or items that were stolen, misappropriated, or withheld by force;
whether they were borrowed personally or lent to others, or exchanged, loaned, or forgotten;
or whether the property of the Triple Gem was used in a confused or mixed manner; or if communal goods such as grain, rice, or firewood [were used improperly]...
Firewood, salt, soybeans, sauces, vinegar, vegetables, fruits, money, silk, bamboo, wood, brocades, banners, canopies, incense,
flowers, oil, and candles— taking these according to one's own whims and desires, whether for personal use, to give to others,
or by plucking flowers from the Buddha’s offerings to use as monastic garlands, one has thus privately misappropriated the property of the Triple Gem.
For the sake of self-interest, such offenses as these have been immeasurable and boundless; today, with shame and remorse, I repent for them all.

Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, we next perform repentance.
Having already completed the repentance for retribution in the hells, we shall now proceed to repent for the retribution of the three evil realms.
As the Buddha said in the sutras:
"A person of many desires, because they seek many gains, also experiences much suffering and affliction.
A person who knows contentment, even if lying upon the bare ground, still considers it happiness;
one who lacks contentment, even if dwelling in heaven, still finds it unsatisfactory."
Yet when people of the world suddenly encounter urgent calamities, they are able to relinquish their wealth without regard for its quantity;
yet they do not realize that this body stands upon the edge of the deep pits of the three miserable realms, and if but a single breath does not return, one shall immediately fall into them.

If a spiritual friend suddenly appears to cultivate merit and virtue for one’s sake, intending to cause them to cultivate the provisions for wholesome dharmas in the future, yet one clings to this stingy mind and refuses to act accordingly—
such a person is utterly foolish and deluded.
Why is this so? In the sutras, the Buddha said:

"At the time of birth, one comes without a single coin; at the time of death, one departs without carrying a single coin. One exhausts the body through accumulation, resulting only in anxiety and distress; it benefits oneself not at all, but serves only the interests of others."
"Having no goodness upon which to rely and no virtue to depend on, our lives have come to their end and we have fallen into the various evil realms.
For this reason, we disciples today prostrate ourselves with bowed heads and, with utmost sincerity, take refuge in the Buddha.
“Disciple, today we shall again repent for the retribution of sins committed within the realm of animals, where there is no conscious awareness.
We repent for the retribution of sins committed within the realm of animals, such as bearing heavy burdens and pulling plows to repay debts from past lives.”
I repent for the retribution of my sins in the animal realm, where I lacked autonomy and was subjected to being hacked, pierced, slaughtered, and dismembered by others.
I repent for the retribution of my sins as a footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed animal.
I repent for the karmic retribution of being devoured by various small insects within the hair, feathers, scales, and shells of my body while in the realm of animals.
Thus, within the realm of animals, there are immeasurable retributions for transgressions; today, with utmost sincerity, I repent for them all.
Next, I further repent for the retributions for long-term hunger within the realm of hungry ghosts.
Repent for the karmic retribution of hungry ghosts who, for hundreds of thousands of millions of years, have never even heard the names of water or broth;
repent for the karmic retribution of hungry ghosts who devour pus, blood, excrement, and filth.
When repenting for hungry ghosts, at the moment the body moves, all the limbs and joints burn with fire as the retribution for one's sins.
When repenting for hungry ghosts, there is the retribution of having a vast belly and a narrow throat.
Thus, regarding the immeasurable retributions of suffering within the realm of hungry ghosts, we today prostrate ourselves and repent for them all.
Next, we further repent for all the deceptions, flatteries, and frauds committed within the realms of spirits, ghosts, and asuras, which constitute their karmic retribution.
I repent for the retribution of my sins within the realm of ghosts and spirits, where I must carry sand and shoulder stones to fill rivers and block seas.
I repent for the retribution of my sins as a rākṣasa or a kumbhāṇḍa, among the various evil ghosts and spirits who devour flesh and blood raw and suffer such hideous deformities.

Thus, for all the immeasurable and boundless retributions of sin within the realm of ghosts and spirits, I today prostrate myself before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the great earth Bodhisattvas, seeking their compassion and repenting so that they may all be completely extinguished.

"May we disciples, by virtue of the merit arising from this repentance for the retribution of animal births and so forth, in birth after birth and life after life, extinguish the defilement of ignorance, recognize our own karmic conditions, possess the clear illumination of wisdom, and sever the bodies of the evil realms."

By the merit produced through this repentance for [the retribution of] hungry ghosts and others, may we, in birth after birth and life after life, forever be free from the suffering of stinginess, greed, and hunger, and always partake of the nectar-like flavor of liberation.

I vow that by the merit produced through this repentance for the retributions of ghosts, spirits, asuras, and others, may I, in life after life and age after age, be upright and sincere without guile; may I be free from the causes of wrong livelihood and eliminate the fruits of ugliness, thereby bringing benefit and blessing to humans and devas.

We, the disciples, vow that from this moment until we reach the site of enlightenment, we shall never again receive the retribution of the four evil realms of existence; we make this exception for when, out of great compassion for sentient beings, we dwell therein by the power of our vows without weariness. [We] prostrate once.
